For a kernel k in L²(μ⊗ν), the operator (Tf)(x) = ∫ k(x,y) f(y) dν(y) from L²(ν) to L²(μ) has adjoint (T*g)(y) = ∫ k̄(x,y) g(x) dμ(x), by Cauchy–Schwarz and Fubini. So T is self-adjoint, when μ = ν, exactly when k(x,y) = k̄(y,x) almost everywhere. It does not say where the symmetry of k comes from, which is [THEORY-009](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-009.md)'s question, and it is not claimed for kernels that are not square-integrable. | Active |
| [CLAIM-293](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-293.md) v3 | The topology of a support graph does not fix how a conclusion should be revised when one of its supports fails: two records with the same edges can carry evidence of different strength and call for different revisions | A6's compensating-evidence case ([CASE-089](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-089.md)), granted against reading [CLAIM-295](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-295.md) as saying a graph of justifications is enough. | [CLAIM-300](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-300.md) v2 | A state sufficient for a family of decisions under a model makes the rest of an inquiry's history worthless for those decisions, and it can stop being sufficient when a source is discredited, the model is revised or the decisions change | A10's answer to the owner's U10, with A8's fourth case and A10's normal constructions ([CASE-082](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-082.md), [CASE-087](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-087.md)). | [CLAIM-305](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-305.md) | Resolving a singularity by blow-up reparametrizes the states and adds no observation, so it cannot make indistinguishable states distinguishable: every point over a singular point gives the same distribution, and the Fisher information can stay degenerate there; what the resolution buys is a normal form for the divergence, and so the learning coefficient | The owner's LEGO monograph says, in Part I (chapters 4, 6, 7, 9, the Overview and "Definitions and Theorems"), that blow-up "restores identifiability", "introduces new observables" and makes the Fisher information non-degenerate, and maps it onto splitting a LEGO bin. | [CLAIM-307](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-307.md) v2 | Retrieval pressure and evidence are different criteria for carving a category, and they move in opposite directions with copy count: evidence that a distinction exists grows with its copies, the search a bin saves shrinks with them, so the bins a deadline forces are often the ones the data least supports | From [MOM-CLM-166](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-166.md), which reads the owner's LEGO parable ([CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md)) against a formalism that cited it with the sign reversed. | [CLAIM-309](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-309.md) | How good a mixture is and how discriminable it is from its diluent come apart: under linear mixing a smoothie's distance from milk only shrinks as milk is added, so a preference that rises and then falls with milk is over the ratio and cannot be a d′, and the signal-detection reading of the owner's smoothie line reverses one of its directions | The smoothie note in the owner's LEGO monograph reads the owner's line ([CASE-096](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-096.md)) as signal detection. Under linear mixing the mixture's taste is (1 − f)s + f·m, and its distance from milk is (1 − f)\|s − m\|. That falls monotonically from the first drop, so discriminability from milk cannot rise and then fall. | [CLAIM-319](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-319.md) v2 | Over a scenario of n contexts in an odd cycle, changing the support of one context takes the contextual fraction from 1 to 0 while the other n − 1 contexts and every marginal are kept exactly, at a weighted observational distortion of 1/n, so within a scenario the fraction's Lipschitz constant against that distortion is at least n; and any change of global extension needs a contextual model on one side | Split from [CLAIM-201](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-201.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the derivation that claim called "decisive and checkable", stated on its own. | [CLAIM-333](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-333.md) | Measuring every relevant variable is necessary but not sufficient for a Granger-causal analysis to say anything about interventions: the intervention must also be an isolated exogenous change and no influence may act within one sampling step, and then Granger noncausality implies no intervention effect and the effect is identified from the observational predictor, but a Granger-causal relation is still only potentially causal | The record's answer to [NOTE-010](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-010.md)'s C5, "if all relevant variables are measured, Granger- and Pearl-type analyses coincide", which the ΦID review asserts without conditions. | [CLAIM-335](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-335.md) v4 | Transfer entropy measures directed predictive improvement, not information flow: as a conditional mutual information it is the source's unique information about the target's next value plus its synergy with the target's past, so it can credit a source with a bit the source carries only jointly and read zero from sources that jointly fix the target, and conditioning on more series does not remove the synergy | The record's position on whether transfer entropy measures information flow. | [CLAIM-340](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-340.md) v2 | Scoring operators on predictions committed before the evidence is not by itself Regime B: in the linearized operator model the coupling of interpretation to conferral has the sign of κ′ − κ̄, so commitment removes capture only when the interpretation bends the reading of the evidence no more than it bends the predictions, and it keeps the learning that revising after the evidence would lose | The formal question [QUESTION-121](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-121.md) asked, answered in [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md)'s linearization ([CASE-106](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-106.md)): is committing predictions before the evidence equivalent to Regime B? | [CLAIM-343](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-343.md) v2 | For three or more parts, no ΦID can use a redundancy function that both satisfies the identity axiom and yields nonnegative atoms, because on the Williams–Beer lattice the two are inconsistent from three sources up; a ΦID verdict on three or more parts therefore rests on which axiom the analyst drops, and should name it | The record's answer to the gap left by the PID filing: no held measure gave ΦID an identity-respecting redundancy for more than two sources. | [CLAIM-345](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-345.md) v2 | Equal controllability rank does not fix the cost of control: for x_{t+1} = x_t + b·u the least quadratic effort for a displacement Δ is Δ²/b², unbounded as b → 0 while the system stays controllable, and in general the least effort is Δxᵀ W_T^† Δx, set by the Gramian and not by its rank | A9 §2 and A12's Proposition 1 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, the step the owner's U9 "controllability of a system isn't binary" needs. | [CLAIM-350](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-350.md) v2 | A coarse-graining preserves a deterministic judgment exactly when the judgment is constant on its fibres: the judgment then factors through the coarse description, uniquely on its image, and otherwise two states the judgment tells apart have been merged | A21 §3 and §18 (Candidate 1) of the exchange of 2026-10-17, and A22's Construction A: for a judgment J and a coarse-graining C on the same states, J = j∘C for some j exactly when C(x₁) = C(x₂) implies J(x₁) = J(x₂). | [CLAIM-351](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-351.md) v3 | A zero aggregate gradient does not show that the demands it aggregates are reconciled: with positive weights it holds both when every demand's own gradient vanishes and when nonzero gradients cancel, and in the second case no update improves them all to first order; even the first is only joint first-order stationarity, which a demand's maximum or saddle also has | A33 §5 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "Zero aggregate gradient does not imply absence of frustrated demands." | [CLAIM-365](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md) v4 | On a norm-ball update set the local frustration residual Φ_r = min over ‖d‖ ≤ r of max_i(ε_i + g_iᵀd) equals the maximum over the simplex of Σλ_iε_i − r‖Σλ_ig_i‖_*, so infeasibility of the declared improvements has a certificate, and any admissible actual update exceeds Φ_r by a nonnegative governance regret | A34 §4 and A35 §3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, checked. | [CLAIM-369](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-369.md) v3 | In symmetric resource-mediated competition with interaction matrix A = UᵀU and growth rates r = Uᵀb − c, Lotka–Volterra population dynamics are multiplicative gradient flow on the convex feature-selection objective ½‖b − Un‖² + cᵀn over the nonnegative orthant: the invasion fitness of an absent component is the negative partial derivative of that objective, and the uninvadable equilibria are its KKT points | From a synthesis the owner relayed on 2026-10-18 (workbench entry of that date), checked here and given a proof. The sharp edge: the identity needs a shared scalar objective, and it fails for asymmetric interactions or processes with competing objectives, which is where an organization stops being an optimizer. | [CLAIM-370](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-370.md) | For a symmetric positive-pair distribution with marginal p, the conditional-expectation operator on L²(p) has the density ratio K⁺ as its kernel, and it is Hilbert–Schmidt exactly when the χ²-divergence of the pair from the product of its marginals is finite, in which case it is compact and self-adjoint with an orthonormal eigenbasis | [THEORY-005](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-005.md)'s derivation, stated as the record's own and with its proof. Johnson et al. ([LIT-258](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-258.md)) write the operator on a finite space without an integrability condition. HaoChen et al. | [CLAIM-372](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-372.md) | Within a fixed measurement scenario, the contextual fraction is a piecewise-linear and Lipschitz-continuous function of the empirical model's probability table, with a constant that depends only on the scenario | The record's own derivation, from the linear programme of Abramsky, Barbosa and Mansfield ([LIT-265](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-265.md), Eq. 3), which [THEORY-165](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-165.md) holds. | [CLAIM-374](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-374.md) | On a consistently connected system, Contextuality-by-Default and the sheaf criterion agree: a maximally connected coupling exists exactly when a global law has the contexts' laws as its marginals | The record's derivation of what [NOTE-600](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-600.md) marks as its own inference. In a consistently connected system, every observable has one distribution in all the contexts that contain it. Then each connection's maximal coupling makes its copies equal with probability 1 ([LIT-777](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-777.md), Theorem 3.3), so a maximally connected coupling is a joint law of one variable per observable, which is a global section in Abramsky and Brandenburger's sense ([LIT-016](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-016.md), [THEORY-012](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md)). Conversely, a global section gives such a coupling. The two criteria come apart only when marginals shift with context. | Active |
| [CLAIM-375](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-375.md) v3 | Under one-hop allocation within an epoch, an operator that grants influence to an ally whose policy is nearer its own than the collective decision is raises how far its preferred policy is realized while its own authority stays fixed, so the two conditions of the grant scheme hold together | The demonstrated core of [CLAIM-285](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md). Under A3's one-hop rule I_j = I_j⁰ + Σ_(k≠j) b_k E_kj, with budgets and baselines fixed within an epoch ([CLAIM-282](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-282.md)), an operator's authority does not respond to its own grants. If the collective decision is the authority-weighted mean of the operators' policies, then granting influence to an ally whose policy is nearer one's own than the decision is moves the decision strictly toward one's policy. So the reward for realized policy, and not for held authority, pays for delegating. It does not say operators behave so, or that any rule beyond one hop keeps both conditions. | Active |
| [CLAIM-376](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-376.md) v2 | A linear system that is stable at every instant can have a positive Lyapunov exponent: shifting any operator with exponent λ > 0 by −δI lowers its exponent by exactly δ and makes every instantaneous operator stable, so for 0 < δ < λ the shifted system is stable at every instant and unstable | The case [THEORY-724](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-724.md)'s source asserts and does not show. If A(t) has first Lyapunov exponent λ > 0, the propagator of A(t) − δI is e^(−δt)Φ(t), so its exponent is exactly λ − δ, while every eigenvalue of every A(t) moves left by δ. Applied to the undamped oscillator switching ω between 0.5 and 3 every unit of time: λ = 0.1955, and with δ = 0.1 the system is stable at every instant, with eigenvalues −0.1 ± 3i and −0.1 ± 0.5i, and has exponent 0.0955. | Active |
| [CLAIM-377](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-377.md) | For any differentiable model under squared loss with Gaussian noise of precision β, the model's Fisher on n inputs is the Gauss–Newton matrix βJᵀJ, and its non-zero eigenvalues are exactly β times those of the empirical NTK Gram matrix JJᵀ, with the same multiplicities, its eigenvectors being Jᵀ applied to the Gram matrix's, normalized | [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md)'s Step 1, stated as the record's own and proved. Through the SVD J = UΣVᵀ, JᵀJ and JJᵀ share the non-zero eigenvalues σ_i² with equal multiplicities, and Jᵀu/σ is the eigenvector of JᵀJ for a unit eigenvector u of JJᵀ. Under y \| x ~ N(f(x; θ), β⁻¹), the expected outer product of the score is β∇f∇fᵀ, which summed over inputs is βJᵀJ, the Gauss–Newton matrix. "Fisher" means the model's Fisher, not the empirical Fisher of observed residuals. It holds at every width, in every regime and on any data. It says nothing about what the spectrum looks like, which is [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md)'s. | Active |
| [CLAIM-378](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-378.md) v2 | A representational similarity index invariant to every invertible linear map depends on a representation only through its column space, so it takes one value on all column-centred representations of rank n − 1, as it does on all representations of rank n | The generalization of [THEORY-236](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-236.md)'s theorem. If col(X) = col(Y), write X = BC and Y = BD with B a basis of the common column space and C, D of full row rank, extend C and D to invertible matrices, and the quotient maps X onto Y. Since XA always has the column space of X, the GL(p) orbits are exactly the sets of n × p matrices sharing a column space. Theorem 1 is the case of column space ℝⁿ. Column-centred matrices of rank n − 1 all have column space 1^⊥, so an invariant index cannot tell them apart either. | Active |
| [CLAIM-379](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-379.md) v2 | On a finite set of stimuli, regularized linear readouts with ridge b > 0 cannot tell apart two centred representations of the same width exactly when one is an orthogonal transformation of the other, and the unregularized CCA member cannot tell apart representations with the same column space, which differ by an invertible linear map | The proved core of [CLAIM-269](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-269.md). What a regularized linear readout decodes is a function of K_X = X G⁻¹ Xᵀ/M, with G = aC_X + bI ([THEORY-008](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md)). For b > 0, K_X and the Gram matrix XXᵀ determine each other, by a monotone map on the shared eigenvalues; and equal Gram matrices mean an orthogonal transformation ([CLAIM-290](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-290.md), [THEORY-004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md)). For b = 0, K_X is the projection onto the column space, which fixes X only up to an invertible linear map, as for a softmax layer ([THEORY-723](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-723.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-380](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-380.md) v2 | With finitely many states and finitely many outcomes, the positive part of the Bayes-risk increase on the same decision problem is directed, is zero from a garbling back to its source, vanishes for every finite problem and prior exactly when the rendering is at least as informative as the source, and has A86's D_Q as its symmetrization | The finite-outcome part of [CLAIM-326](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-326.md). Define D⁺_Q(U → V; π) = sup over q in Q of [r_q,π(V) − r_q,π(U)]⁺, with losses in [0, 1] and a stated prior. A garbling never gains. The term is directed. A86's D_Q is its symmetrization. And with every finite problem and prior, it vanishes exactly when V is at least as informative as U, by Blackwell's Theorem 6 ([THEORY-717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md)). It does not cover outcome spaces that are not finite, or say this is the right decision term. | Active |
| [CLAIM-381](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-381.md) | Over a finite class of items with finite judgement outcomes, a constant outcome kernel fits every item only when the target readers' averaged responses do not vary with the item, an exact fit is a garbling with the item as common parameter, and Le Cam's deficiency and its restriction to finitely many decision problems are finite computations | The derivational core of [CLAIM-228](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md). Over a finite class of items, the target term is the readers' response averaged over a procedure's output, and one outcome kernel family is fixed across the items. Then a constant kernel fits only target responses that carry no information about the item. An exact fit is a garbling, with the item as the common parameter. And Le Cam's deficiency between the two finite tables is one linear programme. Its restriction to finitely many decision problems is a finite computation. It does not say the measure is informative, which is [CLAIM-228](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md)'s empirical question. | Active |
| [CLAIM-383](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-383.md) v3 | In plane Couette and plane Poiseuille flow, measured in the energy norm, the linearized operator about the laminar profile has transient growth at least cR and resolvent norm at least cR² with c independent of R, so wherever it is eigenvalue-stable a perturbation of norm at most CR⁻² makes it eigenvalue-unstable | [THEORY-304](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-304.md)'s scalings as lower bounds, derived. At streamwise wavenumber zero, the cross-stream velocities obey an R-independent Stokes problem in the time t/R. They force the streamwise velocity through −U′v, so the streamwise response is R times an R-independent field. In the energy norm this gives transient growth at least cR, and in the steady forced problem a resolvent norm at least cR². Through pseudospectra, a perturbation of norm O(R⁻²) then moves an eigenvalue into the unstable half-plane wherever the flow is eigenvalue-stable. | [CLAIM-395](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md) | Under Montévil and Mossio's definition of closure, a closed set of constraints has at least two members, and if each constraint is produced at the time scale of a constraint in the set that generates it and not at the scale at which it is itself conserved, the set includes at least one slow and one fast dependence, so a system with a single constraint of its own cannot realise closure |  | Active |

| [CLAIM-399](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-399.md) | Causal abstraction in the senses of Rubenstein et al., Beckers and Halpern, and Beckers, Eberhardt and Halpern does not secure governance-response sufficiency: exact transformation, τ-abstraction and zero approximate-abstraction distance all accept the hidden-bit coarse-graining, which loses ρ(h = 1) bits of the response to h, because each lets high-level noise carry what the coarse state drops; for one outcome and the identity correspondence, sufficiency is their compatibility condition with the high-level context fixed to the coarse state, and strong abstraction rejects the case only through interventions on the hidden parameter | The record's join, on 2026-10-21, of its readings of the causal-abstraction papers ([NOTE-1037](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1037.md), [NOTE-1032](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1032.md), [NOTE-1045](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1045.md)) with [CLAIM-407](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-407.md). A25 of the exchange of 2026-10-20: "We should not present governance-preserving coarse-graining as a new general theory of causal abstraction." That stands. But it is not an instance of these papers' notions either: their criteria compare interventional laws and let the high-level context be any map that works, so they accept the hidden governance bit, whose coarse state keeps nothing of the response to h. Re-checked step by step against the three THEORYs. It corrects [TERM-067](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-067.md)'s first wording, which read the profile as [TERM-043](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-043.md)'s causal component with the identity correspondence. | Active |
| [CLAIM-400](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-400.md) v5 | In the meaning–authority model linearized at symmetry, a third, maintained legibility state that authority moves (ε) and that moves interpretation (ν) or conferral (μ), with persistence λ < 1 and nonnegative couplings, destabilizes the symmetric state exactly when the two-variable condition holds with β + νε/(1 − λ) in place of β and δ + με/(1 − λ) in place of δ: at the threshold the regime is indistinguishable from stronger two-variable couplings, and the slower it is the more it adds, while away from the threshold it adds a mode that no two-variable model has, so a lean in the regime can outlast the advantages it was built from | [QUESTION-253](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-253.md) asked whether authority's effect on what becomes legible as evidence is a third channel with its own instability condition, or [CLAIM-340](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-340.md)'s κ′ renamed. Both, in different respects. With a maintained legibility state r, det(I − J₃) = (1 − λ)[(1 − α)(1 − δ) − βγ] − ε[νγ + μ(1 − α)], which is (1 − λ) times [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md)'s expression with β_eff = β + νε/(1 − λ) and δ_eff = δ + με/(1 − λ). So the instability threshold is a two-variable one with stronger couplings, and a slower regime (λ near 1) adds more. Away from the threshold, r is a third mode: a lean in the regime can hold interpretation and authority off symmetry after they would have relaxed, which no two-variable parameters reproduce. | Active |
| [CLAIM-401](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-401.md) v5 | The conditions an effective description is commonly asked to meet are not of one kind: predictive sufficiency and approximation fidelity are adequacy relative to a declared target, metric and horizon; tractability restricts the operations under which adequacy is assessed; dynamical independence and memory closure are relations of the representation to the system, memory relative to a chosen projection; so a matrix over them as independent binary axes conflates kinds | A4 and A5 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U4 ("it sounds like considering it from this angle has potentially already altered our characterization of those 'virtues'"). A4: "(P) and (A) look increasingly like evaluation criteria, while (D) and (M) describe different aspects of system–representation structure. (C) describes resource accessibility." A5: approximation fidelity "may specify the degree to which a prediction or dynamical relation is preserved", and tractability "can instead restrict the operations over which preservation is evaluated". | [CLAIM-407](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-407.md) v4 | A coarse-graining exactly informationally closed under a process's ordinary dynamics need not preserve its responses to an intervention on the mechanism: for a declared intervention distribution ρ, independent of the state, the deficiency Γ = I(S; Y^(I) \| T(S), I) can be positive, as in the hidden governance bit, where it is ρ(h = 1) bits; and Γ = 0 exactly when, for every intervention ρ charges, the response kernels are constant on T's fibres over the states of positive probability | A16 §3–4 of the exchange of 2026-10-20 and A17 §4.2–4.3, its paper's Proposition 1, reused at A18 and in A23's audit. The qualitative point was on file: [CLAIM-350](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-350.md)'s "What it does not say" (A22's Construction B of 2026-10-17, [CLAIM-127](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-127.md)), and [CLAIM-122](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-122.md)'s supervisory test, whose note of 2026-10-18 has it without parameters. | [CLAIM-408](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-408.md) v3 | In ḋ = (α − κ)d − βd³, with d the difference between two parties' shares of authority, α their self-reinforcement and κ a constraint that bears on both alike, the equal allocation is the only equilibrium and is stable for κ > α, and for κ < α it is unstable and the unequal allocations ±√((α − κ)/β) are stable: a constraint that favours neither party can, by weakening, destabilize the equal allocation and make persistent unequal allocations stable, of any size near the threshold (\|d*\| → 0 as κ → α), without determining which party gains the larger share, and in this model restoring κ > α restores the equal allocation | A19 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U19: does the account "capture 'deregulation' as a disguised effort to induce organizational symmetry breaking?" | [CLAIM-409](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-409.md) v3 | For one state law, one intervention distribution and one outcome, a deficiency of sufficiency cannot increase under refinement: if T₁ = g∘T₂ then Γ(T₂) ≤ Γ(T₁); informational closure, by contrast, is monotone in neither direction, since in the three-bit chain of Rosas et al. | [CLAIM-414](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-414.md) v4 | Matched ordinary trajectories can conceal differences in an interpretation's efficacy, in the allocation of that efficacy, and in the maintenance of its enabling constraints: in two finite constructions, systems that agree under ordinary operation differ in each, and a specified intervention exposes the difference that passive observation of the matched trajectories does not | A10 of the exchange on experience and interpretation, re-run here. Under an intervention that sets it to 1, the first never acts on it, the second acts at once, and the third acts one step late, because its own interpretation opens the gate. A single perturbation runs one into (0,0) and leaves the other restored to (1,1): one maintains its constraints by [CLAIM-395](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md)'s minimal slow–fast closure, the other is reset from outside. These are [CLAIM-407](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-407.md)'s lesson about governance and [CLAIM-194](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-194.md)'s about boundaries, applied to interpretation. | Active |
| [CLAIM-434](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-434.md) | On a finite set of outcomes, some function rises with every move that wins one of a negotiation's conflicts exactly when no chain of winning moves returns to where it began, and the length of the longest such chain ending at an outcome is one such function; a perfectly transitive record of which side won each pair, in a complete tournament contesting every pair once, leaves a cyclic share of (n − 2)/3n under the Hodge decomposition, a baseline that does not carry to sparse records; the Hodge gradient can reverse a comparison the wins settle, netting a record erases alternation, a record fixes a class of potentials rather than one, a coherent record is not yet one aligned with any single perspective's ordering, a best-fitting ordering of a cycle is no Lyapunov function, the sign a class of potentials gives can be set-valued, and an ordering fitted to a record overstates its agreement there | The formal core of the rename of 2026-10-23 from "ascendancy" to "potential" ([TERM-076](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-076.md)). Part 1 is the finite case of Monderer and Shapley's equivalence between the finite improvement property and a generalized ordinal potential, proved here because the record has not read their paper ([LIT-1462](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1462.md)). Part 2 is a calibration of the Hodge decomposition (Candogan et al.; Jiang et al.) for binary conflict records, computed here: even a perfect ranking leaves a cyclic residual. Part 3 separates coherence from alignment. Parts 9 to 11 were added after a second review. Parts 4 to 8 were added when a review of the pull request found that the measures built on parts 2 and 3 confused ordinal and cardinal structure; each is checked in scratch/formal/valence.py. | Active |
| [CLAIM-436](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-436.md) v5 | An instantaneous ordering is a common currency on a finite set of options, where every complete preorder has a real-valued representation, but not in general: the lexicographic order on the unit square has no real-valued representation, while a continuous complete preorder on a connected separable space has a continuous one; so admitting an ordering is strictly weaker than admitting a currency, a graded lexicographic override lies in the gap while an exact threshold override does not, a threshold override with a discrimination threshold is a lexicographic semiorder whose choices can cycle and so is no ordering at all, and even where each instant has a currency, successive currencies need not share exchange rates | The formal half of the owner's reframing of 2026-10-23, that a "common currency" is better read as a negotiation admitting an (at least instantaneous) ordering. On finite option sets the two coincide at each instant. On a continuum they do not: a graded lexicographic order, one form ALARM's "100% weight" override could take, admits no numerical representation, while a continuous ordering, the form of Veit's proportional trade-offs, admits a continuous one (Eilenberg; Debreu). A threshold override admits a discontinuous one, and one with a discrimination threshold, a lexicographic semiorder, can cycle and admits no ordering at all (Luce; Tversky). Across instants, representations need not be related, so a sequence of currencies need not be one currency. | Active |
| [CLAIM-452](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-452.md) v2 | For an organization whose response in each probe context is the authority-weighted mixture of its processes' known response profiles, the authority shares are identifiable from a set of contexts exactly when the processes' stacked profiles over those contexts are affinely independent; because the response is linear in the shares, local and global identifiability coincide, the condition is that the Fisher information of any design supported on those contexts is positive definite on the simplex's tangent space, and with binary outcomes at least one context fewer than there are processes is needed | When an organization's response in context c is p_π(·\|c) = Σᵢ πᵢ pᵢ(·\|c), the mixture [CLAIM-444](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-444.md) reduces the replicator model to, which probe contexts reveal its authority shares π? Exactly those over which the profiles are affinely independent. The response is linear in π, so there is no gap between local and global identifiability, and the condition is the Fisher information of [CASE-159](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-159.md)'s pullback being positive definite on the tangent space of the simplex. Each binary context adds at most one rank, so k processes need at least k − 1 contexts. It is a condition checkable before any data, which is what [QUESTION-031](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-031.md) asks for; none of the three works read on 2026-10-25 states it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-455](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-455.md) | For one bounded observer, a transformation of a representation can make one task's distinction legible and another's illegible at once, so legibility regimes are ordered only relative to a task, and a regime that improves one perspective's competence can disable another's | Stated in [CASE-154](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-154.md)'s title and its "What it can show" and held by no claim, found in the audit of 2026-10-27 for propositions cases state that no claim holds. With two fair bits and an observer that reads one coordinate and cannot compute XOR, the raw pair gives 50% error on the XOR task and 0% on the first bit, and the XOR gives the reverse. [CLAIM-199](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-199.md) says a garbling can raise usable information for a receiver; this adds that the same garbling lowers it for another task of the same receiver. The edge: one observer, two tasks; nothing about which task matters. | Active |
| [CLAIM-459](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-459.md) | An input to a bistable balance of authority can be sincere and causally efficacious without changing which regime operates: below a threshold the structure of the competition sets, it moves the balance within the current basin, so a higher-order volition that changes nothing visible need not be idle | Stated in [CASE-112](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-112.md)'s title and its first "What it can show" bullet and held by no claim, found in the audit of 2026-10-27. In ẇ = μw − w³ + h with μ > 0, the operative regime changes only when \|h\| passes 2μ^{3/2}/(3√3); for 0 < h < h_c the input moves w and leaves the regime. A8 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "An endorsement can be sincere and causally efficacious while remaining too weak to shift the system out of its current attractor basin." The edge: efficacy on the balance, not on behaviour; the claim says a null in behaviour is no evidence of a null input. | Active |
| [CLAIM-463](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-463.md) | Restoring the conditions under which a capacity was lost need not restore the capacity: where the activity that maintains it reinforces itself, the same conditions can sustain both the capacity and its absence, so a capacity lost past a threshold returns only under conditions better than those it was lost under, or by rebuilding the activity directly, and restoring it can cost more than preserving it would have | A4's claim candidate from the exchange "About the Chagossians" of 2026-10-26, "Resource restoration does not imply organizational restoration", which the first filing declined because [CASE-111](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-111.md) already derives it; the owner asked for it to be filed as a claim with its connection to the case. Demonstrated by [CASE-111](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-111.md)'s normal form: in the bistable range, returning the parameter to its pre-collapse value leaves maintenance at zero. The edge: a possibility shown in a model, not a finding about any grant program, people or institute, and a slow recovery is not evidence of the threshold. | Active |
| [CLAIM-480](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-480.md) v2 | Composing interactions can turn an interior into a constraint, and sometimes into a constraint of a new kind: in the chain E = ½k₁(x₁ − x₂)² + ½k₂(x₂ − x₃)², with x₂ internal and equilibrated, the boundary sees E_eff = ½·k₁k₂/(k₁ + k₂)·(x₁ − x₃)², a coupling between x₁ and x₃ that neither part has; if the interior relaxes slowly, eliminating it leaves a history-dependent constraint, a memory kernel, so interconnection fixes an effective constraint on the boundary's trajectories and separation of time scales decides only whether that constraint is approximately memoryless; and for cellular sheaves the reduced constraint can relate three boundary values where every relation among the parts is pairwise | From A22 §4 and A23 §IV of the exchange of 2026-10-27, which called composition "the most important missing mechanism" after the owner's U20. Eliminating an equilibrated interior leaves an effective boundary relation that no part has; an outside system interacting only with the boundary meets it as a constraint, and "The interior has effectively become apparatus." Baez and Fong's black-boxing functor is the general theorem for passive linear networks. The memory case ties it to Mori–Zwanzig and to [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md): interconnection yields an effective constraint on the boundary's trajectories in every case, and separation of time scales decides only whether it is approximately memoryless. For cellular sheaves the reduction can need a richer relational vocabulary than the parts used (THEORY-1090; QUESTION-283). It is independent evidence for [CLAIM-477](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-477.md), that constraints are realized by organization. | Active |
| [CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md) v3 | Coupling does not by itself separate time scales: two identical undamped oscillators coupled with stiffness k have normal modes at ω₀ and √(ω₀² + 2k), nearly equal when k ≪ ω₀², and neither decays; separation comes where the coupling dissipates relative differences faster than collective ones, as in ẋ = −ax − k(x − y), ẏ = −ay − k(y − x), whose collective and relative modes relax at rates a and a + 2k, and in a Laplacian flow ẋ = −κLx, where the spectrum of L sets the rates | The answer A20, A21 and A23 gave to the owner's conjecture at U20 that coupling necessarily induces scale separation ([CLAIM-473](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-473.md)). Two small computations: conservative coupling splits modes without separating or damping them, and dissipative coupling damps the relative mode at a rate that grows with the coupling. For a Laplacian flow the kernel is exact compatibility and the nonzero spectrum is the hierarchy of relaxation rates, so a spectral gap is where the separation comes from. Conceded, so Active. It gives a mechanism for [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md)'s second half and is not a test of individuality. | Active |
| [CLAIM-495](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-495.md) | For an O(d)-valued connection on a connected graph, the assignments that meet every edge relation xᵢ = Tᵢⱼxⱼ form a space isomorphic to the vectors at one vertex fixed by every holonomy based there, which is the kernel of the connection Laplacian; for d = 1, and for U(1) phases, that space is all or nothing, but for d > 1 a connection whose loops are not trivial can still keep a subspace on which every loop is, so compatibility among local frames can be partial and graded by direction; and edge maps that do not commute can compose to a flat loop, so non-commutativity is not holonomy | From A2 and A3 of the exchange "Paper assessment" (2026-10-29), which drew it out of [LIT-1820](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1820.md)'s O(d) setting against [THEORY-1082](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1082.md)'s U(1) one. The proof and the example are the record's, checked numerically. It is the zeroth cohomology of the connection sheaf, so standard, and it says nothing about which organizations have such transports. | Active |
| [CLAIM-496](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-496.md) | Agreement between routes of translation is a measure of coherence, not of fidelity, and the two are independent: a rendering that sends every source utterance to one output makes direct and relay transport agree exactly while a receiver who could tell a promise from a prediction with no error is left at chance, and two routes that keep the act and differ in register disagree completely while losing nothing the act-identification task needs | From A4 and A5 of the exchange "Paper assessment" (2026-10-29), where the assistant carried [LIT-1820](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1820.md)'s comparison of alternative paths over to translation and then warned that "path agreement is a coherence criterion, not a fidelity criterion". The constructions are the record's. It does not say path discrepancy is uninformative: it says it measures something [CLAIM-259](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md)'s directed loss does not, and conversely. | Active |
| [CLAIM-497](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-497.md) v2 | A system's causes are found at the coarsest description whose interventions are unambiguous: a macro description is causally proportionate where it merges only micro states that intervention cannot tell apart, and no coarse-graining carries more causal information than the micro description it supervenes on | The record's position on causal emergence after [THEORY-787](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-787.md) was rejected. A coarse-graining can be the right causal description, but not by beating the micro. Under one intervention distribution at both levels, no coarse-graining of a transition carries more effective information than its micro ([THEORY-1167](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1167.md)). The ones that lose nothing are exactly causal feature learning's partitions, which merge only micro states with the same interventional effects ([THEORY-1169](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1169.md)). The step from there to "the causes are found at the coarsest such description" is the record's own, in the sense of proportionality. It does not say the macro adds causal information. | Active |
| [CLAIM-502](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-502.md) v2 | Multi-hop delegation can keep an operator's authority exactly independent of its own grants: under leave-one-out damped delegation, which counts the authority reaching each operator only along paths that have not already passed through it, an operator's grants raise the authority of every operator its grantee reaches and leave its own unchanged | A construction that shows [CLAIM-282](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-282.md)'s old title false. Compute each operator's authority from A2's damped recursive rule with that operator's own outgoing grants removed. Then authority reaches it along paths of any length, but only along paths that have not passed through it, so nothing it grants can return to it. Its authority is exactly independent of its own grants, and a grant moves authority two hops and more. It does not say the rule conserves authority, that it closes the social route of moving others' grants, or that [CLAIM-375](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-375.md)'s guarantee carries over. | Active |
| [CLAIM-503](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-503.md) v2 | Over finitely many states and finite outcome sets, one experiment is ε-deficient relative to another in every decision problem with losses in [0, 1] exactly when a single Markov kernel brings it within ε in total variation at every state, so the deficiency computed as a linear programme is the least such ε | Le Cam's randomization criterion for finite experiments, uniform in the state, with losses in [0, 1]. The least ε for which some kernel brings M within ε of N in total variation at every state, which [CLAIM-381](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-381.md) computes as a linear programme, equals the least ε for which M is ε-deficient relative to N in every finite decision problem. One direction composes N's rule with the kernel; the other is one minimax step over a bilinear objective. At ε = 0 it is the finite Blackwell order ([THEORY-717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-515](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-515.md) v2 | Whether an organization has a cognitive property is four questions, not one: what information about the property can be recovered from its behaviour, what capabilities it can actually exercise, what mechanisms realize them, and whether it can maintain or transform those mechanisms; the four can come apart, and none should be silently substituted for another | The general principle the owner drew at the second review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): "When asking whether an organization 'has' a cognitive property, distinguish the information recoverable from its behavior, the capabilities it can actually exercise, the mechanisms realizing those capabilities, and its ability to maintain or transform those mechanisms." It was drawn from the world-model case ([CLAIM-514](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-514.md)) and judged "sufficiently general—and sufficiently testable—that it deserves an explicit place in Nucleation's research program". Interpretive: its instances are demonstrated case by case, and the generalization is not. | Active |
| [CLAIM-516](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-516.md) | Where every constraint capacity turns over at a positive rate and is produced only by others, with no basal production and production vanishing as its producers do, capacities whose production graph is acyclic all decay to zero: a capacity that persists needs a productive cycle among its ancestors, and removing a feedback edge set extinguishes every capacity; a cycle is necessary and not sufficient, and a one-member cycle is not closure | From A10 §1 and §5A of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), after the owner's "try to progress the theoretical program". The proof was rechecked by the reader of U7–U10. It is known in substance from autocatalytic-set theory, as A10 said. What it adds to the record is the boundary with closure: the necessary cycle may be a self-loop, and a self-loop is not closure in [TERM-070](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-070.md)'s sense or [CLAIM-395](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md)'s, which need two or more constraints. | Active |
| [CLAIM-517](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-517.md) | A successor regulator keeps a viable set positively invariant if, at every boundary context, its response distribution is within γ/L in total variation of a regulator that certifies inward margin γ, the dynamics being L-Lipschitz in that distribution; an average distillation loss certifies this only through coverage of the boundary contexts, so fidelity measured in ordinary operation certifies nothing about viability | From A16 §4 and §5 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), the owner having quoted its conclusion at U17: "preserving a regulator's response distribution sufficiently accurately can guarantee preservation of a physical organization's viability". The algebra was rechecked; the regularity conditions A16 left implicit are stated here. A16's application to its own construction (γ = 0.16) was notional, since that model has no regulator distribution and L is undefined there. | Active |
| [CLAIM-521](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-521.md) v2 | An organization's present coupling strength need not reveal the stability of the process maintaining it: in a constructed system whose maintained connector and capacities set a three-unit coupling, the recovery rate of the maintenance goes to zero at its saddle-node while the coupling's spectral gap there stays near 0.989 | From A12 §6 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), which called it "a surprising result". It is generic for any saddle-node whose fold sits away from zero with no feedback from the coupled units to the maintaining core, so it is built in rather than surprising. It is filed because it is a construction [QUESTION-125](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-125.md) asks for: one in which the regime changes while the block's gap does not. All numbers were recomputed. | Active |
| [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md) v4 | Recovery under interventions on state cannot show where maintenance is realized: an outside controller that measures the constraint capacities and supplies the internal production law as state feedback yields the same trajectory under every perturbation of state, damage and recovery included, even with every capacity observed exactly; only interventions on the production mechanisms, relative to a declared boundary, separate the two | From A10 §4 (its Proposition 5) of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31). Close to definitional, and checked: substituting the controller gives the same differential equation. It extends [CLAIM-414](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-414.md) from passive observation to every intervention on state. As the reader noted, the causal dependence among the capacities is the same in both systems; only where the mechanism sits relative to the boundary differs, which is [CLAIM-194](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-194.md)'s point about boundaries. | Active |
| [CLAIM-524](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-524.md) | Whether functionally equivalent realizations are connected depends on which paths are admissible: for f = u₁v₁ + u₂v₂ with nonnegative weights, (1, 1, 0, 0) and (0, 0, 1, 1) are joined by a curve along which f stays 1 though the straight line between them falls to ½, and under any resource budget below √2 times the endpoints' cost no path with f = 1 joins them | From the owner's remark at U17 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), that the reconstruction fibres "reminds me of loss landscape connected mode stuff (which might just be a consequence of high dimensional geometry? ... probably already discussed on the nucleation record)". It is: see below. A17 §9 gave the curve and A18 §7 the budget for a tied-weight family; the general bound here is the reader's, rechecked. "Viable mode connectivity" is A18's name and is not filed as a term. | Active |
| [CLAIM-528](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-528.md) v2 | That a mechanism realizes a capacity can mean that the capacity is produced through it over time or that the capacity consists in it at a time, and interventions show only the first: a pathway whose disabling changes the capacity after a delay is a cause, can be intervened on surgically, and can be located relative to a declared boundary, whereas every intervention on a capacity that consists in its parts also changes some part along another path, so that relation is underdetermined by intervention data and is inferred by abduction or from simultaneity and settled parthood; and which of the two a given dependence is depends on the time resolution at which a description treats the parts' response as instantaneous | Filed on reading the fat-handedness debate after Craver: Baumgartner & Gebharter 2016, Baumgartner & Casini 2017 and Baumgartner, Casini & Krickel 2020. It says what their result does and does not reach in the record. [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s conclusion is causal and is left standing; [CLAIM-515](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-515.md)'s "realized", read synchronically, is not shown by discriminating interventions; and the debate's own line between causation and constitution, simultaneity, moves with the time scale, as [CLAIM-480](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-480.md)'s chain shows. It does not say that constitution is unknowable, or that the record's organizations have constituents in the mechanists' sense. | Active |
| [CLAIM-530](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-530.md) v3 | Where maintenance is realized is a question of constitutive relevance only through its parthood condition: an internal producer and an outside controller supplying the same production law as state feedback meet mutual manipulability's two manipulability conditions identically, since disabling or stimulating either changes the maintained capacities and intervening on the capacities changes the activity of either, so what puts one inside and the other outside is parthood, a boundary the experiments presuppose and do not find | The record's join of [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md) with the mechanist account of constitution, from Craver and Bechtel's admission that interlevel experiments are symmetrical and show componency only prima facie ([THEORY-1287](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1287.md)). In [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s pair the bottom-up and top-down interventions come out alike for producer and controller. So the criterion separates them only by its parthood clause, which is [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s declared boundary. The criterion is cited as Baumgartner and Gebharter state it (LIT-1934, p. 8, read in full in NOTE-1493); Craver's own texts stay unread. It does not say no criterion can draw the boundary. Closure, a producer that is itself maintained by what it produces, is a candidate that [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s one-variable model cannot express. | Active |
| [CLAIM-535](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-535.md) v4 | An organization that acts on what it observes has a policy acceptable in every circumstance exactly when, for each observation, the circumstances it cannot tell apart share an acceptable action; so every circumstance having an acceptable action does not give a policy, a finer observation never removes one, and where acceptable actions overlap the coarsest observations that suffice are several and incomparable, so which distinctions must be made legible depends on which acceptable action the organization commits to | A33 §4 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), at the owner's U33 request for positive accounts, with A30 §2's example and A32's Claim B. Its second appearance in the exchange, so it gets a code. The criterion is elementary, and its monotonicity is Blackwell's easy direction ([THEORY-1096](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1096.md)). What it adds to [CLAIM-350](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-350.md), its single-valued case, is found by the reader of U32–U33: with overlapping acceptable sets, legibility is relative to policy. A positive characterization of what legibility must supply for action. | Active |
| [CLAIM-536](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-536.md) v3 | A categorical model of perspectives and an LDA-style model differ in where the mixture lives: the first draws every act's perspective from one fixed categorical distribution, the second gives each episode its own mixture, drawn from a Dirichlet, and draws each act from it; the Dirichlet is a distribution over mixtures, not the perspectives themselves, and with symmetric concentration a over K perspectives two acts in one episode share a perspective with probability (a + 1)/(Ka + 1) against 1/K across episodes, so the concentration runs from one perspective per episode, as in persona selection (a → 0), to a fresh independent draw for every act (a → ∞) | The owner's U12 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), stated precisely: "H1 isn't LDA like though. that's my point. it's a categorical distribution. the topics in H@ are the dirichlet distribution which parameterizes the categorical distribution, which is what distinguishes H2 from H1 and why H2 is an LDA." The structure is right; one word is not. The Dirichlet is a distribution over each episode's mixture, and the topics, here the perspectives, are the categories that mixture weights. The agreement formula, derived here and checked by simulation, shows that both readings of H1 are limits of H2. | Active |
| [CLAIM-537](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-537.md) v2 | In tolerance-bounded compatibility on a graph with disturbed offsets, \|Dx − a₀ − w\| ≤ δ for \|w_e\| ≤ η_e, a compatible configuration exists for every disturbance exactly when \|cᵀa₀\| + Σ η_e\|c_e\| ≤ Σ δ_e\|c_e\| on every cycle, and one configuration serves every disturbance exactly when η ≤ δ and \|cᵀa₀\| ≤ Σ(δ_e − η_e)\|c_e\|; an agent that chooses its configuration from what it observes needs the second condition within each class of disturbances it cannot tell apart, so whether a compatible state can be selected lies between the two and depends on what the agent can read | A30 §§2–3 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), at the owner's "keep going", with the second and third conditions derived by the reader of U30–U31 and checked by simulation (500 random instances, no mismatch). It is the first concrete instance of the branch's note of 2026-11-02 on [CLAIM-354](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-354.md), that a reachable set should range over the policies an organization can carry out on what it can read. The framing is adjustable robust optimization ([LIT-1975](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1975.md)). Static selection only, scalar overlaps only. | Active |
| [CLAIM-538](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-538.md) | On a finite graph of contexts whose overlaps carry preferred real offsets a and tolerances δ_e ≥ 0, an assignment within every tolerance, \|Dx − a\| ≤ δ, exists exactly when no cycle's holonomy exceeds the sum of its tolerances; with every δ_e > 0 the least uniform enlargement of the tolerances that admits one is the largest ratio, over simple cycles, of holonomy to summed tolerance, so the obstruction is certified by a cycle; the feasible allocations of tolerance depend on the offsets only through their class in H¹, so local adjustment can move a mismatch among the overlaps of a cycle and never remove it; and an evaluation that omits one overlap of every witnessing cycle reports a compatibility that does not hold | The owner's U27 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), "compatibility of tolerance bounds", with U28's pointer to the record's sheaf tools, worked out at A28 §3 and A29 §§3–4, 7 and A32's Claim A. The feasibility criterion is the classical feasible-differential theorem of network flows (Rockafellar 1984; no checked identifier, not registered), and the ratio is LP duality, so the result is granted, not the record's discovery. What the record adds is the reading: the frontier is an invariant of the obstruction class, governance chooses where on it the mismatch falls, and omission can fake compatibility. Checked by linear programming against brute-force cycle enumeration on random graphs. | Active |
| [CLAIM-540](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-540.md) | The persistence a Dirichlet–categorical hierarchy gives a run of selections is an observer's learning about a fixed mixture, not a change in what selects: under a uniform prior an observed first choice raises the predicted chance of repeating it from 1/2 to 2/3, while the same choice forced leaves it at 1/2, so the hierarchy's reinforcement is not evidence of self-formation or of a maintained will-organization, which need the mixture itself to change under the choice | A13 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), answering the owner's U13, what the Dirichlet–categorical reading implies for Jennings's attention as the source of a free will. A13: "Self-formation requires a causal update, not merely a posterior update in the observer." Correct, short and not held. It limits the record's own H1/H2 reading ([CLAIM-536](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-536.md)) and A11's suggestion that LDA already has "a primitive analogue of a will-organization". Rechecked here by simulation. | Active |
| [CLAIM-542](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-542.md) v2 | Sensitivity does not fix the allocation or the authorship of control: linearized, every input reaches the final state through the same transition operator, ∂x_T/∂w_t = Φ(T, t)B_w(t), so systems with the same Lyapunov spectrum can differ arbitrarily in what an agent's own channel, an outside party's channel and noise each reach and at what least energy; and along one unstable direction a larger exponent λ lowers the least effort to reach a displacement, since W_T = b²(e^{2λT} − 1)/2λ grows with λ, while a constant open-loop input against white noise entering the same direction has terminal signal-to-noise ratio tending to (bu/σ)√(2/λ), which falls as λ grows, so only feedback that observes the state turns cheaper control into reliable direction | The demonstrated part of the owner's U16 and U20 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), "controllability vs sensitivity". A20 §2 stated the impulse case ("the relative contribution is not determined by e^{λT}") and A22 §5 the channel case. The scalar signal-to-noise result is the reader's derivation, checked by simulation.
